title: The Broken Veil
premise: Sable Amberdale has spent their whole life in the Veilless Valley, the one place where magic cannot follow, stealing memories from travelers to survive and never asking why they were left there as a child. When the crown of Aldermarch declares a hunt for all gifted souls, Sable learns they are the last heir of the Amberdale line — the family that forged the covenant binding the human realm to the fae Otherworld, and whose broken oath is now tearing the Veil apart. Hunted by the crown's memory-eating inquisitors and guided by a disgraced fae knight named Corvane, Sable must gather three shattered covenant-stones hidden across the realms before the next eclipse seals the Veil forever. At the eclipse, Sable discovers the final stone is their own stolen childhood memories, willingly given up by their mother to hide them; by returning them and choosing to belong to both worlds at once, Sable reforges the covenant at the cost of ever being fully one thing or the other.
about_author: Mirabel Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing forgotten family letters before turning to fantasy. They write about inheritance, half-belonging, and the stories families refuse to tell, from a drafty house full of unlabeled boxes.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable lifts a merchant's memory of the sea outside the valley, savoring a world they've never seen, then returns to their hovel above the pawnshop. Establishes the valley's magic-dead nature and Sable's hunger for belonging. Emotional beat: longing disguised as competence.

chapters.title: A Buyer With Empty Eyes
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A hooded stranger pays gold for a specific memory — a lullaby Sable doesn't recognize but somehow knows. The stranger's eyes hold no reflections, and when they leave, frost blooms indoors despite the valley's dead magic. Emotional beat: first crack in Sable's safe little world.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Crown criers announce the Gifted Purge: anyone with magic will be taken for 'examination.' The pawnshop keeper who raised Sable burns papers and finally admits Sable was left on his doorstep wrapped in a sigil-marked cloth. Emotional beat: shelter becoming a cage.

chapters.title: What Follows Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Inquisitors breach the valley — something that should be impossible — led by the memory-eater Wren Vael. The pawnshop keeper dies buying Sable time to flee through the old quarry tunnels. Emotional beat: grief and guilt fused into forward motion.

chapters.title: The Knight in the Briars
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Outside the valley for the first time, Sable collapses as ambient magic floods senses trained to nothing. They're found by Corvane, an exiled fae knight bound to guard the Amberdales, who recognizes the sigil cloth. Emotional beat: overwhelming wonder edged with terror.

chapters.title: Heir of a Broken Oath
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Corvane explains the covenant: the Amberdales bound both realms together, then broke it a generation ago, shattering the Veil into leaks. Three covenant-stones can reforge it before the eclipse. Sable refuses — until Vael's hunters crest the ridge. Emotional beat: resentment of an inheritance never chosen.

chapters.title: The Road of Borrowed Faces
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Fleeing through a border town where fae glamours run rampant, Sable steals memories to disguise themselves and Corvane, discovering their gift works on fae too — something no thief should manage. Emotional beat: the gift is stranger and larger than theft.

chapters.title: Wren Vael's Offer
chapters.summary: Vael's POV. The inquisitor corners Sable privately, revealing she was once a gifted child 'examined' by the crown and hollowed into a weapon. She offers Sable a place beside her: help her find the stones, and she'll let the valley go. Emotional beat: seeing your possible future in your enemy.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The first covenant-stone lies in a chapel sunk in a fen, guarded by a memory-ward that traps intruders in their worst recollection. Sable walks through their own — the night they were abandoned — and takes the stone. Emotional beat: surviving your worst memory changes you.

chapters.title: Corvane's Shame
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Around the fire, Corvane confesses he was the covenant's sworn guardian who failed to stop its breaking — because he loved Sable's mother and obeyed her final order to look away. Emotional beat: two people carrying different halves of the same guilt.

chapters.title: The Court of Thorns Refuses
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Seeking fae alliance, they petition the Thorn Court, which blames humans entirely for the Veil's collapse and sentences Sable to death as an oathbreaker's heir. Only the queen's forgotten debt to the Amberdales buys a reprieve: one favor, no more. Emotional beat: belonging offered only as a transaction.

chapters.title: Stolen From the Stealer
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Vael ambushes them and rips a decade of Sable's stolen memories away, leaving gaps where skills and friendships used to be. Corvane anchors Sable by recounting their journey back to them, memory by memory. Emotional beat: identity held together by someone else's witness.

chapters.title: The Mountain That Remembers
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The second stone sleeps inside a living mountain that replays the covenant's forging. Sable witnesses their ancestors' oath — and their mother's face among the witnesses, pregnant, terrified. Emotional beat: history becoming personal.

chapters.title: Mother's Letter
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Within the mountain's echo, Sable's mother's recorded message plays: she broke the covenant deliberately to hide Sable, whose dual-blooded nature would have made them the crown's perfect weapon. She gave Sable's earliest memories to the third stone to seal them away. Emotional beat: fury and love indistinguishable.

chapters.title: The Choice at Thornhold
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Vael captures the second stone and offers it back if Sable surrenders. Sable instead trades the Thorn Court's owed favor to Vael — freedom from the crown's control — turning their enemy into a wary ally. Emotional beat: spending your only leverage on mercy.

chapters.title: Eclipse Eve
chapters.summary: Vael's POV. With hours left, the three converge on the Veil's central tear, where reality thins and the dead whisper. Vael reveals the crown's true plan: not to seal the Veil but to weaponize it. The army arrives behind them. Emotional beat: enemies standing shoulder to shoulder against a worse enemy.

chapters.title: The Battle of the Fraying
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Crown forces, fae renegades, and our trio clash at the tear while the eclipse begins. Corvane holds the line at terrible cost; Vael turns her hollowing gift against the crown's own inquisitors. Emotional beat: sacrifice without guarantee.

chapters.title: The Third Stone Is You
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. At the tear's heart, Sable finds the third stone — and understands it is the vessel of their own returned infancy, held by the Veil itself since their mother's bargain. Taking it means reclaiming everything, including the pain. Emotional beat: the self as the final key.

chapters.title: What Was Given Up
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable takes the memories back: a mother's voice, a fae father's laugh, the forging ritual learned in the cradle. Whole for the first time, they begin the reforging even as the crown's siege engine tears the sky. Emotional beat: grief and wholeness arriving together.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. Sable speaks the covenant anew — not as a wall between realms but a door with obligations on both sides — fusing the three stones with their own dual blood. Corvane and Vael anchor them against the backlash. The Veil knits closed as a luminous seam. Emotional beat: transcendence bought with vulnerability.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Two Worlds
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The crown's hunt collapses; the new covenant grants gifted humans sanctuary and fae accountability. Sable declines both thrones' offers, keeping the stones as a neutral wardenship. Emotional beat: peace that doesn't require erasing yourself.

chapters.title: The Door Left Open
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, epilogue. A year later, Sable tends the Veil-seam from a cottage straddling both realms, teaching other dual-blooded children. Corvane stays; Vael sends word of a new threat stirring far north. Sable opens the door and steps toward it. Emotional beat: belonging chosen daily, adventure continuing.
